result.summary: The diagnosis matches the code: every keystroke refetches the same term-independent incident list and 429s are retried inside a per-minute limit, but the PR only shrinks how many pages each search reads. It leaves the refetching and 429 retries in place, so a team sharing one API key will still hit the limit, and it quietly cuts name search from 2,500 to 750 incidents for a workspace with about 8,000.

problems.title: Same list is refetched on every keystroke
problems.detail: The list request ignores the search term, so every debounced query downloads identical pages. A short per-connection cache would remove most calls; capping pages only lowers the cost per keystroke.

problems.title: 429 still retried three times
problems.detail: The default retry rule retries 429 with Retry-After: 1, so all retries land in the same 60-per-minute window and use up more of the budget. The PR names this as a cause but leaves it unchanged.

problems.title: Name search coverage cut from 2,500 to 750
problems.detail: The target workspace has around 8,000 incidents (INC-6201, INC-8193 in fixtures), so older incidents can no longer be found by name. The description presents this as preserved behaviour rather than a product trade-off.

problems.title: Rate limit is shared across the workspace
problems.detail: One Nango connection means one incident.io key for every agent, so 3 calls per non-matching query still runs out at about 20 queries a minute across the team.

problems.title: Undisclosed trim change
problems.detail: Matching now uses the trimmed term, so whitespace-only queries count as empty and fetch one page. This is not mentioned in the description or covered by a test.

problems.title: Tests restate the constants
problems.detail: The tests check call counts of 1 and 3 but not matches adding up across pages, the trim change, or any 429 behaviour.

result.betterFix: Cache the list pages per connection for about a minute and filter in memory, and don't retry 429 on this interactive path; return a rate-limited error instead. Then keep the wider coverage, since it no longer costs extra calls.
